newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Kelian expects 1996 gold production of 14 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Kelian expects 1996 gold production of 14 tonnes.

text.p: PT Kelian Equatorial Mining, Indonesia's biggest gold mine, expects to produce around 14 tonnes of gold this year compared to 11.8 tonnes in 1995, the company's president director John Pegler said on Tuesday.
"We expect to produce around 14 tonnes of gold this year," he told Reuters.
He said output from the open-pit mine, located in the foothills of the Central Kalimantan mountains in East Kalimantan, was 11.8 tonnes last year.
"There was a throughput problem with the plant last year which has been overcome. There was also some low grade areas as part of the mining schedule last year as well," Pegler said.
Kelian is 90 percent owned by RTZ-CRA and 10 percent by Indonesia firm PT Harita Jayaraya.

While Kelian is the biggest purely-gold mine in the country, copper-gold producer PT Freeport Indonesia -- 82 percent owned by the U.S. Freeport-McMoran Copper and Gold Inc -- expects to produce between 49.5 and 52.6 tonnes of gold this year, Freeport Vice President Paul Murphy told Reuters on Tuesday.
RTZ-CRA also has a 12 percent equity stake in Freeport-McMoran.
Pegler said Kelian's output was expected to remain at between 13 and 14 tonnes a year through its anticipated life span to the year 2003.
Asked if there was any possibility of extending the mine's life, he said: "We'll actively explore around the mine over the next year or so and there is some possibility."
The mine began commercial production of gold in January 1992.

A company brochure said it had proved ore reserves of 35.8 million tonnes with a grade of 1.27 grammes of gold per tonne, and probable ore reserves of 8.2 million tonnes with a grade of 1.68 grammes per tonne.
